newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean blue chip stocks close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Chilean blue chip stocks close slightly lower.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed slightly lower in brisk trading, as baragin-hunters looked to take advantage of the recent weaknesss, traders said.
The bolsa is expected to open higher Monday and should remain buoyant for most of the week, they said.
"People are starting to buy, but we will have to wait and see if it is sustained. Much will depend on external factors," said Pedro Santa Maria, finance manager at brokerage Socimer,
The selective IPSA index ended off 0.02 percent at 96.06 points. The general IGPA index declined 0.09 percent to 5,302.46 points.
Turnover was 11.3 billion pesos, with buying by mutual funds and private investors setting the pace, traders said.

Investors are looking ahead to the release next week of Chile's August inflation rate and fresh U.S. employment data, said traders. The consensus sees Chilean consumer prices rising 0.5 percent in August, said dealers.
"August and September are traditionally high-inflation months, so people are watching these figures especially carefully," said one trader.
Consumer prices rose 1.6 percent in August last year and 0.6 percent in September 1995.
Gainers included glassmaker Cristales, up 0.69 percent at 2,920 pesos, bottler Andina, up 0.68 percent at 2,235 pesos, and steel company Cap, which rose 0.61 percent to 1,310 pesos.

Losers included pension fund manager Provida, down 1.61 percent at 9,150 pesos, forestry firm Masisa, down 1.02 percent at 195 pesos, and copper products company Masisa, which lost 0.53 percent to 930 pesos.
